data.topic: Auto-detection, self-learning, and auto-memory systems for AI coding agents — conflict detection, self-learning memory, autonomous coordination, trust calibration, auto-review loops
data.input_summary: Integrate parallel coordination, smart merge queue, agent health monitoring, auto-review loops, and graduated autonomy into the dotclaude orchestration pipeline, removing epic-level serialization and enabling cross-epic story parallelism

decisions.choice: Hybrid approach: git merge-tree first pass (fast, language-agnostic), escalate to semantic check on detected conflicts to filter false positives from textual proximity
decisions.reasoning: Balances speed with precision. Git merge-tree catches real conflicts without parser maintenance. Semantic escalation only fires on flagged conflicts, keeping the common path fast. Informed by Grove's 5-layer approach but adapted to our Python/Shell stack.

decisions.choice: Priority queue with dependency locking: stories merge as soon as they pass tests if they don't share write-targets with stories ahead of them. Non-conflicting stories skip the queue.
decisions.reasoning: Maximizes throughput without FIFO bottleneck. Quickfixes don't wait for refactors. Uses existing write_files tracking in epics.db. Informed by Overstory's FIFO queue but with smarter ordering.

decisions.choice: Dual-gate monitor: background watchdog parsing live agent logs for repetition patterns (same tool call with identical args) + soft token/time budget
decisions.reasoning: Catches the known Haiku replace loop pattern and similar stuck states without killing valid long-running architect tasks. Combines precision of pattern detection with safety net of resource limits.

decisions.choice: Layered: global trust score as baseline + domain-scoped overrides auto-created on divergence (3+ domain-specific failures while global is green). Same pattern as correction→preference pipeline.
decisions.reasoning: Don't preemptively track every domain. Derive domain tags from write-target paths automatically. Graduation gates check min(global, domain) so domain failures can lower trust but global can't override them. Consistent with the lazy-layer memory philosophy.

decisions.choice: Ralph Loop-style stop hook re-injection with dual-exit-gate (completion indicators + explicit EXIT_SIGNAL) and circuit breakers (no-progress threshold, same-error threshold)
decisions.reasoning: Proven pattern across Ralph Loop, Aider --auto-test, BugBot. Overbaking mitigated by bounded iterations and progress detection. Integrates naturally with our existing stop hook infrastructure.

decisions.choice: Remove epic-level serialization entirely. Conflict checking operates at story level via write-target overlap, regardless of epic membership. Epics remain grouping only.
decisions.reasoning: Epics are organizational, not execution boundaries. The real constraint is write-target conflicts between stories, and pm_check_conflicts already checks this. Just need to extend it across all in-progress stories, not just same-epic.

constraints.value: Must stay within Claude Code primitives (skills, hooks, MCP tools, background agents)
Must use existing epics.db (SQLite) for state — add tables, don't replace
Must integrate with existing OpenMemory for learning persistence
Must work with current worktree-based coder isolation
SQLite WAL mode + retry policy needed for concurrent agent writes to epics.db
Rate limit awareness: central concurrency manager or token guard for parallel agents
State recovery protocol for watchdog-killed agents: auto-revert worktree and re-queue vs manual intervention
